name: NF4 Quantization Codec Specification
description: Specification for implementing a blockwise NormalFloat4 quantization codec with double quantization, C extension packing, and binary checkpoint I/O.

nf4_map.description: The NF4 data type uses 16 quantization levels derived from quantiles of N(0,1). The asymmetric layout has 7 negative levels, zero, and 8 positive levels (with +1.0 as boundary). This is information-theoretically optimal for normally distributed data.

construction.right_tail: Generate 9 evenly-spaced values from offset to 0.5 (inclusive endpoints). Evaluate the inverse CDF of N(0,1) at the first 8 of these 9 points. Since all quantile points exceed 0.5, these produce 8 positive values.
construction.left_tail: Generate 8 evenly-spaced values from offset to 0.5 (inclusive endpoints). Negate the inverse CDF values at the first 7 of these 8 points. These produce 7 negative values.
construction.assembly: Combine the 8 positive values, 0.0, and the 7 negative values (16 total). Sort ascending. Normalize to [-1, 1] by dividing all values by the maximum absolute value.

nf4_map.tolerance: Each computed value must match the reference within 1e-3 absolute error.

quantize.step_1: Divide input data into consecutive blocks of blocksize elements. The last block may have fewer elements.
quantize.step_2: For each block, compute absmax = max(|v| for v in block). This is the symmetric scaling factor. For all-zero blocks, absmax = 0.
quantize.step_3: For each value v in the block: if absmax == 0, map to the NF4 index closest to 0. Otherwise, normalize: n = v / absmax, then find the NF4 index i that minimizes |n - nf4_map[i]|.
quantize.step_4: Store the list of indices (4-bit, 0-15), the list of per-block absmax values, the blocksize, and the original element count.

blockwise_quantization.dequantize: For element i: block_index = i // blocksize; reconstructed = nf4_map[indices[i]] * absmax[block_index]

double_quantization.description: Reduces memory overhead of absmax scaling constants from 32 bits to approximately 8 bits per block.

quantize.step_3: Divide centered values into inner blocks of inner_blocksize.
quantize.step_4: For each inner block: compute inner_absmax = max(|v| for v in inner_block).
quantize.step_5: Quantize: q = clamp(round(127 * centered / inner_absmax), -127, 127). If inner_absmax == 0, q = 0.

bnb_pack_nibbles.signature: void bnb_pack_nibbles(const uint8_t* indices, uint8_t* out, int count)
bnb_pack_nibbles.description: Packs count 4-bit indices into bytes. First index in low nibble, second in high nibble.

bnb_unpack_nibbles.signature: void bnb_unpack_nibbles(const uint8_t* packed, uint8_t* out, int count)
bnb_unpack_nibbles.description: Unpacks count 4-bit indices from packed bytes.

bnb_packed_size.description: Returns ceil(count / 2), the number of bytes needed.

c_extension.integration: Load the compiled .so via ctypes.CDLL. Set argtypes and restype for each function. Use ctypes arrays for data transfer.

crc32.description: CRC32 (zlib.crc32) of all preceding bytes (header + body). Stored as unsigned 32-bit little-endian.

benchmark_data.format: Flat binary array of float32 values, little-endian
benchmark_data.description: Normally distributed model weights for benchmarking the blocksize evaluator

optimal_blocksize.description: Given input data, a list of candidate block sizes, and a maximum mean absolute error budget: find the largest blocksize (most memory-efficient) whose quantization error does not exceed the budget.
optimal_blocksize.algorithm: Sort candidates in descending order (largest first). For each candidate: quantize and dequantize the data, compute mean absolute error (MAE). Return the first (largest) candidate with MAE <= error_budget. If no candidate meets the budget, return the smallest candidate.
optimal_blocksize.rationale: Larger blocksizes use less memory but produce higher quantization error. This function finds the best compression-accuracy tradeoff.
